description: We are developing an Mars navigation platform for astronaut EVAs. It combines NASA elevation, surface-imagery, and rover-hazard data to create detailed 3D terrain models, assess route traversability, detect slope hazards, and maintain communication line-of-sight awareness for safer tactical exploration.
summary: We developed Project AresPath, an intelligent navigation and environmental situational awareness engine built for future human Martian explorers. Using real datasets from NASA, ESA, and ISRO, the platform transforms orbital data into an interactive, multi-resolution 3D Mars globe.  AresPath directly addresses the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge by bridging the gap between orbital planning and ground-level execution. Users can analyze slope and roughness maps, compare Shortest, Balanced, and Safest rover routes by distance and elevation gain, and drop to a 2.5-meter eye-level 360° viewpoint to preview terrain with a Cinematic Replay before taking a step.  The tool is important for human space exploration because safe traversal on Mars requires understanding both macro-level geography and micro-level surface hazards. By allowing mission planners and astronauts to rehearse extravehicular activities (EVAs), evaluate steep climbs, and inspect real Martian craters and ridges from the crew’s perspective, Project AresPath reduces operational risk and enhances survival on the Red Planet in hopes of pushing humanity towards Martian exploration.
details:
Project AresPath: 3D Martian Terrain & Route Explorer

AresPath is an interactive 3D Mars globe and surface route planner built on real NASA, USGS, and ESA elevation datasets. It lets users explore Mars from orbit down to meter-scale terrain, analyze surface slopes, plan 3D routes, and experience ground-level views right in the browser.

Note

Live Demo & Resolution Disclaimer
The hosted demo runs a low-resolution version of the terrain data due to cloud hosting storage and resource allocations—the full high-resolution dataset is ~15 GB. As a result, terrain detail on the live site will not look nearly as sharp as the visuals shown in our presentation. To experience the full high-resolution terrain, run the data pipeline locally to download the datasets directly to your machine.

Key Features

  • Multi-Resolution 3D Mars Globe: Streams real elevation data on demand as you zoom—combining global MOLA (~14.8 km), the USGS HRSC/MOLA Global Blend (200 m), and high-resolution CTX (20 m) & HiRISE (~1 m) terrain at Jezero Crater, Gale Crater, and Olympus Mons.
  • 3D A∗ Route Planner: Pick any two points (or search 2,051 official Mars landmarks) to calculate and compare Safest, Balanced, and Shortest paths using real terrain slope constraints and an interactive elevation profile.
  • Cinematic Route Replay: Pre-loads high-resolution terrain along your chosen route using Web Workers and IndexedDB for a smooth, terrain-following camera fly-through.
  • Surface 360° & GPU Path Tracing: Stand 2.5 m above the Martian surface at any point with progressive multi-bounce GPU path-traced lighting.
  • Real-Time NASA Sky (RT) & 33 Visual Filters: Uses NASA NAIF SPICE kernels (spiceypy) to render live Martian sun/star positions alongside real-time overlays for slope, elevation, roughness, contours, and data resolution.

Tech Stack

  • Frontend: JavaScript (ES Modules), Vite, Three.js, three-gpu-pathtracer, three-mesh-bvh, Web Workers, IndexedDB
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, Rasterio / GDAL, NumPy, SpiceyPy (NASA CSPICE)
  • Data Sources: NASA MGS MOLA, USGS HRSC/MOLA 200m Blend, NASA MRO HiRISE & CTX DTMs, IAU/USGS Planetary Gazetteer, JPL DE440s & HEASARC BSC5P Star Catalog

1. Install Dependencies

python -m pip install -r backend/requirements.txt
cd frontend && npm ci && cd ..

2. Prepare Terrain & Sky Data (First Run)

python -m pip install -r pipeline/requirements-terrain.txt
python pipeline/verified_terrain.py --sites jezero gale
python pipeline/stitch_globe.py
python pipeline/expand_gale.py
python pipeline/prepare_olympus_detail.py
python pipeline/prepare_sky.py
# Optional (~11.4 GB global 200 m layer):
# python pipeline/prepare_global_terrain.py

3. Run the App

npm run dev

  • 3D Mars Explorer: http://127.0.0.1:5173/
  • Tile Inspector: http://127.0.0.1:5173/tiles.html
  • API Docs: http://127.0.0.1:8001/docs

4. Run Tests

npm test
python -m pytest backend/tests -q

Project Structure

  • frontend/ — Vite + Three.js 3D globe, shaders, route UI, cinematic replay, and 360° surface viewer
  • backend/ — FastAPI tile server, A∗ route planner, and SPICE sky calculator
  • pipeline/ — Scripts to download and verify official NASA/USGS datasets
